title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第47部分：搜索引擎

chapters.Engine: 14. 为小说打造的搜索引擎
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

72f9649f77a0.en: How do you find the ten most useful pages among hundreds of billions, in a fraction of a second? <bookmark mark='a'/> The first search engine, Archie, written at McGill University in 1990, indexed the names of files on FTP servers, not their contents. By 1994 there were crawlers and directories of the web, and in 1995 AltaVista searched the full text of the web, quickly. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1998 Sergey Brin and Larry Page described Google, which treated links between pages as votes, and began with an index of twenty-four million pages. <bookmark mark='c'/> Today's indexes hold hundreds of billions of pages, and rank them with learned models and dense vectors as well as words.
72f9649f77a0.zh: 如何在几分之一秒内，从几千亿个网页中找出最有用的十个？<bookmark mark='a'/>第一个搜索引擎 Archie 于1990年在麦吉尔大学写成，它索引的是 FTP 服务器上的文件名，而不是文件的内容。到1994年，已经有了网络爬虫和网页目录；1995年，AltaVista 能快速地搜索整个网络的全文。<bookmark mark='b'/>1998年，谢尔盖·布林（Sergey Brin）和拉里·佩奇（Larry Page）描述了 Google：它把网页之间的链接当作投票，起步时的索引有2400万个网页。<bookmark mark='c'/>今天的索引容纳几千亿个网页，给它们排序时，除了词，还要用学习得到的模型和稠密向量。

f36b35a4395c.en: A search engine rests on five ideas, and each is a piece of mathematics this series has met. <bookmark mark='a'/> An inverted index turns a query into the merging of sorted lists. <bookmark mark='b'/> Compression keeps those lists small enough to hold in memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> A probabilistic model of what relevant means produces the ranking formula called BM25. <bookmark mark='d'/> A random surfer wandering over links produces PageRank. <bookmark mark='e'/> And vectors place documents near queries that mean the same thing, found by searching a graph.
f36b35a4395c.zh: 搜索引擎建立在五个思想之上，每一个都是这个系列遇到过的一段数学。<bookmark mark='a'/>倒排索引把一次查询变成对有序列表的合并。<bookmark mark='b'/>压缩让这些列表小到可以放进内存。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个关于“相关”含义的概率模型，给出了名为 BM25 的排序公式。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个在链接之间漫游的随机冲浪者，给出了 PageRank。<bookmark mark='e'/>而向量把文档放在意思相同的查询附近，并通过在一张图上搜索找到它们。

9d682e233e25.en: In this part we build one, for the thirty novels of this series. <bookmark mark='a'/> The novels are cut into 11,261 passages of four hundred words, and indexed: 40,692 distinct terms, 2,364,691 postings. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ask it for the white whale, and it ranks the passages, and shows each with a snippet around the words that matched. <bookmark mark='c'/> By the end of the part every step of that will be ours: the tokenizer, the index, the compression, the ranking, and an evaluation of how good the ranking is.
9d682e233e25.zh: 在这一部分里，我们为这个系列的30部小说建造一个。<bookmark mark='a'/>小说被切成11261个400词的段落，并建立索引：40692个不同的词项，2364691个倒排项。<bookmark mark='b'/>向它查询 white whale，也就是白鲸，它就给段落排序，并为每一段显示匹配词周围的一段摘要。<bookmark mark='c'/>到这一部分结束时，其中每一步都会是我们自己的：分词器、索引、压缩、排序，以及对排序好坏的评估。

6b6689b1d941.en: This is Part 47 of Computer Science, Built. <bookmark mark='a'/> We will fit Zipf's and Heaps' laws to the novels; build an inverted index and intersect its lists with as few comparisons as possible; compress them with codes whose lengths we derive; derive BM25 from a model of relevance and measure it; skip most of the work with WAND; rank pages by a random walk; find near-duplicates; and search by meaning, with vectors compressed by product quantization and searched by a layered graph.
6b6689b1d941.zh: 这是计算机科学，从零搭建，第47部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会在小说上拟合齐普夫定律和 Heaps 定律；建立倒排索引，并用尽可能少的比较求它的列表的交集；用长度由我们推导出来的编码压缩这些列表；从一个相关性模型推导出 BM25，并测量它；用 WAND 跳过大部分工作；用随机游走给网页排序；找出近似重复；还要按意思搜索，向量用乘积量化压缩，再通过一张分层的图来搜索。

bf97aa771b52.en: Chapter one. Words, stems and Zipf.
bf97aa771b52.zh: 第一章：词、词干与齐普夫。

9800163b9a94.en: A search engine sees characters, and its first job is to decide what the words are. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our tokenizer keeps runs of letters and digits and folds them to lower case, so that Whale at the start of a sentence and whale in the middle become one term. Folding has a price: it also merges US, the country, with us. <bookmark mark='b'/> Next come stop words, forty-eight short words such as the, of and a. In Jane Austen's first sentence they are twelve of the twenty-three tokens. Our index keeps them, because phrases need them, but ranked queries drop them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Last, stemming cuts each word down to a stem, so that acknowledged, acknowledges and acknowledging all become one term.
9800163b9a94.zh: 搜索引擎看到的是字符，它的第一项工作是确定哪些是词。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的分词器保留连续的字母和数字，并把它们转成小写，这样句首的 Whale 和句中的 whale 就成了同一个词项。大小写折叠是有代价的：它也把国名 US 和 us 合并了。<bookmark mark='b'/>接下来是停用词，48个短词，比如 the、of 和 a。在简·奥斯汀（Jane Austen）的第一句话里，它们占了23个词元中的12个。我们的索引保留它们，因为短语查询需要它们，但排序查询会把它们丢掉。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后，词干提取把每个词削成一个词干，于是 acknowledged、acknowledges 和 acknowledging 都变成同一个词项。

34ce853cc40a.en: Martin Porter published his stemmer in 1980, and it is still in wide use for English. <bookmark mark='a'/> It uses no dictionary: about sixty suffix rules in five steps, applied in order. Follow generalizations. Step one strips the plural. Step two turns ization into ize, step three turns alize into al, and step four removes the al, leaving gener. <bookmark mark='b'/> A rule may fire only if enough of the word would remain. Porter measures a stem by counting its vowel-consonant pairs: gener has two, so its al can go, but riv has only one, so rival keeps its ending. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our implementation reproduces all twenty of the published examples. It merges whaling and whales into whale, and connection, connected and connecting into connect. <bookmark mark='d'/> It also errs: general and generous both become gener, and ran never meets run. A lemmatizer, with a dictionary of word forms, would fix both, at a price.
34ce853cc40a.zh: Martin Porter 在1980年发表了他的词干提取器，至今仍广泛用于英语。<bookmark mark='a'/>它不用词典：大约60条后缀规则，分5步，按顺序应用。跟着 generalizations 走一遍。第一步去掉复数。第二步把 ization 变成 ize，第三步把 alize 变成 al，第四步去掉 al，剩下 gener。<bookmark mark='b'/>一条规则只有在词剩下的部分足够长时才能触发。Porter 用元音—辅音对的个数来度量一个词干：gener 有两对，所以它的 al 可以去掉；而 riv 只有一对，所以 rival 保留词尾。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的实现重现了全部20个已发表的例子。它把 whaling 和 whales 合并成 whale，把 connection、connected 和 connecting 合并成 connect。<bookmark mark='d'/>它也会出错：general 和 generous 都变成 gener，而 ran 永远遇不到 run。词形还原器带着一部词形词典，能修正这两个问题，但要付出代价。

471cc81fe1fe.en: Now count. The thirty novels hold four and a half million tokens, and sixty-one thousand seven hundred and twenty different words. <bookmark mark='a'/> The commonest, the, occurs two hundred and thirty thousand times: one token in twenty. The top twenty words make up almost a third of all the text. <bookmark mark='b'/> Plot frequency against rank, both on logarithmic scales, and the points fall close to a straight line. That is Zipf's law: George Kingsley Zipf described it in the 1930s and 1940s, with frequency roughly proportional to one over the rank. Fitted between ranks ten and ten thousand, our line has slope minus one point two one. <bookmark mark='c'/> At the other end, twenty-two thousand eight hundred and eighty-eight words, more than a third of the vocabulary, occur exactly once. So an index must handle a few enormous postings lists and a vast number of tiny ones, both cheaply.
471cc81fe1fe.zh: 现在来计数。30部小说共有450万个词元，61720个不同的词。<bookmark mark='a'/>最常见的 the 出现了23万次：每20个词元就有一个。前20个词占了全部文本的将近三分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>把频率对排名作图，两个轴都取对数刻度，点就落在一条直线附近。这就是齐普夫定律：George Kingsley Zipf 在20世纪30和40年代描述了它，频率大致与排名的倒数成正比。在排名10到1万之间拟合，我们的直线斜率是负1.21。<bookmark mark='c'/>在另一端，22888个词，超过词汇表的三分之一，恰好只出现一次。所以索引必须既能廉价地处理少数巨大的倒排表，也能廉价地处理数量庞大的极小倒排表。

76e97eb3d799.en: How fast does the vocabulary grow as we read? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the number of different words seen, against the number of tokens read, novel after novel. It climbs steeply, then ever more slowly, but it never levels off: every book brings new names and new words. <bookmark mark='b'/> Gustav Herdan, and later Harold Heaps, described this as a power law: the vocabulary grows as a constant times the number of tokens to a power beta. Our fit gives beta of nought point four eight five, close to a half, so a hundred times the text brings about ten times the vocabulary. <bookmark mark='c'/> The jump at the end is Ulysses, last in our order, and the richest in new words. <bookmark mark='d'/> Stemming cuts the vocabulary by a third, to forty thousand six hundred and ninety-two terms. Those terms are the dictionary of the next chapter.
76e97eb3d799.zh: 我们读得越多，词汇量增长得有多快？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是见过的不同词的数目，对读过的词元数作图，一部小说接一部小说。它先陡峭上升，然后越来越慢，但从不趋于平坦：每本书都带来新的名字和新的词。<bookmark mark='b'/>Gustav Herdan，以及后来的 Harold Heaps，把它描述为一个幂律：词汇量的增长等于一个常数乘以词元数的 β 次方。我们拟合得到的 β 是0.485，接近二分之一，所以文本增加到100倍，词汇量大约增加到10倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>末尾的跳跃是《尤利西斯》（Ulysses），它在我们的顺序中排在最后，新词也最丰富。<bookmark mark='d'/>词干提取让词汇量减少三分之一，降到40692个词项。这些词项就是下一章的词典。

6e1fe372e532.en: Without an index, every query must read all four and a half million tokens of the novels. <bookmark mark='a'/> Picture instead a table with a row for every term and a column for every passage, marked where the term occurs. For our novels that is forty thousand six hundred and ninety-two rows by eleven thousand two hundred and sixty-one columns: four hundred and fifty-eight million cells. <bookmark mark='b'/> Only two point three six million are marked, about half of one per cent. <bookmark mark='c'/> So keep only the marks: for each term, the sorted list of passages that contain it, called its postings. The text, turned on its side, has become an inverted index: from words to passages.
6e1fe372e532.zh: 没有索引，每次查询都必须读完小说的全部450万个词元。<bookmark mark='a'/>不妨想象一张表：每个词项一行，每个段落一列，在词项出现的地方做上标记。对我们的小说来说，这是40692行乘11261列：4.58亿个格子。<bookmark mark='b'/>其中只有236万个被标记，大约百分之零点五。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以只保留标记：对每个词项，保留包含它的那些段落的有序列表，叫作它的倒排表（postings）。文本侧过来，就变成了一个倒排索引：从词到段落。

cc80ac80efef.en: An inverted index has two parts. <bookmark mark='a'/> The dictionary holds every term with its document frequency, the number of passages that contain it, and the place where its list begins. Whale is in three hundred and ninety passages, Ahab in a hundred and eighty-one. The dictionary can be a hash table, from Part 17, or a sorted tree, which also allows prefix searches. <bookmark mark='b'/> The postings hold passage numbers in increasing order, each with the positions where the term occurs. The next chapters rely on that order: sorted lists merge, and neighbours are close. <bookmark mark='c'/> Whale begins with a run, passages six hundred and fifty-nine to six hundred and sixty-nine: the opening of Moby-Dick, with its pages of quotations about whales. Words cluster, and clusters compress.
cc80ac80efef.zh: 倒排索引有两部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>词典保存每个词项，连同它的文档频率，即包含它的段落数，以及它的列表开始的位置。whale 出现在390个段落里，Ahab 出现在181个段落里。词典可以是第17部分的哈希表，也可以是一棵有序的树，后者还支持前缀搜索。<bookmark mark='b'/>倒排表按递增顺序保存段落编号，每个编号都带着词项出现的位置。后面几章都依赖这个顺序：有序列表可以合并，相邻的编号彼此接近。<bookmark mark='c'/>whale 以一串连续的编号开头，从段落659到669：那是《白鲸》（Moby-Dick）的开头，有好几页关于鲸的引文。词会聚集，而聚集的东西可以压缩。

7958b61ebf5e.en: How is the index built? The simplest way is to sort. <bookmark mark='a'/> Read the passages in order, and write down a pair for every term in each: the term and the passage number. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sort the pairs by term, and within a term by passage. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now each term's pairs sit together, and reading them off gives its postings, already in order. The novels make two point three six million pairs; at eight bytes a pair, that is nineteen megabytes, one sort in memory. <bookmark mark='d'/> A crawl of the web makes far more pairs than any memory holds. So sort as many as fit, write each sorted block to disk as a run, and merge the runs: Part 16's external sort, unchanged. This is blocked sort-based indexing.
7958b61ebf5e.zh: 索引是怎么建起来的？最简单的办法是排序。<bookmark mark='a'/>按顺序读段落，为每个段落里的每个词项记下一对：词项和段落编号。<bookmark mark='b'/>把这些对按词项排序，同一个词项之内再按段落排序。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在每个词项的对都挨在一起，依次读出它们，就得到它的倒排表，而且已经有序。小说产生236万对；每对8字节，就是19兆字节，在内存里排一次序就够了。<bookmark mark='d'/>一次网络爬取产生的对，远远多于任何内存能容纳的数量。所以能装下多少就排多少，把每个排好序的块作为一个归并段写到磁盘，再合并这些归并段：原封不动的第16部分的外部排序。这就是基于块的排序索引构建。

8fb517e69af3.en: Blocked sorting needs a table from every term to an integer, kept in memory throughout, and it sorts pairs that could have been grouped as they arrived. <bookmark mark='a'/> Single-pass in-memory indexing, described by Steffen Heinz and Justin Zobel in 2003, uses a hash table instead. Each term maps to a growing list, and because passages arrive in order, every list is born sorted. <bookmark mark='b'/> When memory fills, the terms are sorted, the block is written to disk, and the table starts again, empty. <bookmark mark='c'/> At the end, all the blocks are merged at once, as in Part 16. Our own builder is this algorithm with a single block: one pass over every passage.
8fb517e69af3.zh: 分块排序需要一张从每个词项到一个整数的表，并且始终留在内存里；而且它要排序的那些对，本可以在到达时就分好组。<bookmark mark='a'/>单遍内存式索引构建，由 Steffen Heinz 和 Justin Zobel 在2003年描述，改用一个哈希表。每个词项映射到一个不断增长的列表，而且因为段落按顺序到达，每个列表生来就是有序的。<bookmark mark='b'/>内存满了，就把词项排序，把这个块写到磁盘，然后表清空，重新开始。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后，像第16部分那样，一次性合并所有的块。我们自己的构建器就是只有一个块的这个算法：对每个段落只扫一遍。

6d29124ca8b7.en: Real collections change. <bookmark mark='a'/> New documents go into a small index in memory, searched beside the others, and when it fills it is written out as a segment. <bookmark mark='b'/> Segments of equal size are merged, like the carries of a binary counter, so each posting is copied only a logarithmic number of times. <bookmark mark='c'/> Deleted documents are marked in a bitmap, and dropped at the next merge. Lucene, the library beneath Elasticsearch and OpenSearch, keeps its index as immutable segments merged in much this way: the design of Part 34's log-structured merge trees.
6d29124ca8b7.zh: 真实的文档集合会变化。<bookmark mark='a'/>新文档进入内存中的一个小索引，与其他索引并排被搜索；它满了，就作为一个段写出去。<bookmark mark='b'/>大小相同的段会被合并，就像二进制计数器的进位，所以每个倒排项只被复制对数次。<bookmark mark='c'/>被删除的文档在一个位图里做标记，并在下一次合并时丢掉。Lucene 是 Elasticsearch 和 OpenSearch 底下的库，它把索引保存为不可变的段，大体就以这种方式合并：这正是第34部分日志结构合并树的设计。

e6da97a1709e.en: A query for whale and sea wants the passages on both postings lists. <bookmark mark='a'/> Because both lists are sorted, one walk finds them. Keep a finger on each list and compare the two numbers. If they are equal, that passage is an answer, and both fingers move on; if not, the finger on the smaller number moves. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every comparison moves at least one finger, so the walk costs at most the sum of the two lengths. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same walk computes OR, keeping everything it passes, and AND NOT. With more than two terms, begin with the shortest lists, because an intersection can only shrink.
e6da97a1709e.zh: 查询 whale 和 sea，要的是同时出现在两个倒排表上的段落。<bookmark mark='a'/>因为两个列表都有序，走一遍就能找出它们。在每个列表上各放一根手指，比较两个数。如果相等，这个段落就是一个答案，两根手指都前进；如果不等，指着较小数的那根手指前进。<bookmark mark='b'/>每次比较至少让一根手指前进，所以这一遍的代价至多是两个列表长度之和。<bookmark mark='c'/>同样的走法也能计算 OR，保留它经过的一切，以及 AND NOT。超过两个词项时，从最短的列表开始，因为交集只会越变越小。

6ca1e0aa61ff.en: When one list is much longer than the other, most of the walk along it is wasted. <bookmark mark='a'/> So add shortcuts. In a list of n postings, every square-root-of-n-th posting also points square root of n places ahead. Before stepping, check the shortcut: if its target is still no larger than the other list's current passage, jump. <bookmark mark='b'/> The square root balances the costs: more shortcuts take more space and more checks, and longer ones overshoot more often. Alistair Moffat and Justin Zobel studied skips in compressed postings in 1996. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the novels, the AND whale drops from eleven thousand one hundred and thirty-seven comparisons to one thousand seven hundred and ninety.
6ca1e0aa61ff.zh: 当一个列表比另一个长得多时，沿着它走的大部分路程都是浪费。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以加上捷径。在一个有 n 个倒排项的列表里，每隔根号 n 个倒排项，就有一个同时指向前方根号 n 处。前进之前先查看捷径：如果它的目标仍不大于另一个列表的当前段落，就跳过去。<bookmark mark='b'/>平方根平衡了两种代价：捷径越多，占的空间和要做的检查就越多；捷径越长，越过头的次数就越多。Alistair Moffat 和 Justin Zobel 在1996年研究了压缩倒排表中的跳跃。<bookmark mark='c'/>在小说上，查询 the AND whale 的比较次数从11137次降到1790次。

5b2fe61c9044.en: Galloping, from Part 24, goes further. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take each passage of the short list in turn and look for it in the long list: probe one place ahead, then two, four, eight and sixteen, doubling until a probe overshoots. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then binary search the last gap. Jon Bentley and Andrew Yao described this unbounded search in 1976. <bookmark mark='c'/> Finding m items in a list of n this way costs about m times the logarithm of n over m, far less than the walk when m is small. The AND whale now takes one thousand four hundred and eighteen comparisons, and love AND marriage one thousand nine hundred and fifteen, against two thousand six hundred and eighty for the merge.
5b2fe61c9044.zh: 第24部分的倍增查找走得更远。<bookmark mark='a'/>依次取短列表里的每个段落，在长列表里找它：向前探1个位置，然后2个、4个、8个、16个，不断加倍，直到某次探测越过头。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后在最后一段间隔里做二分查找。Jon Bentley 和 Andrew Yao 在1976年描述了这种无界查找。<bookmark mark='c'/>用这种方法在长度为 n 的列表里找 m 个元素，代价大约是 m 乘以 n 除以 m 的对数，当 m 很小时远少于逐个走。the AND whale 现在只需1418次比较；love AND marriage 需要1915次，而合并需要2680次。

a52155530eee.en: Here are all three on five queries over the novels. <bookmark mark='a'/> When the two lists are of similar length, like whale and sea, or Elizabeth and Darcy, the merge or skips win, and galloping wastes its probes. <bookmark mark='b'/> When one list is five or twenty-nine times longer, galloping wins, nearly eight times over for the AND whale. <bookmark mark='c'/> So engines choose by the ratio of the lengths, or use adaptive algorithms, like those of Erik Demaine, Alejandro López-Ortiz and Ian Munro, which do well on any mix. And comparisons are not the whole cost: Part 24's branch-free loops and SIMD instructions, comparing several ids at once, matter as much.
a52155530eee.zh: 这是三种方法在小说的5个查询上的表现。<bookmark mark='a'/>当两个列表长度相近时，比如 whale 和 sea，或者 Elizabeth 和 Darcy，合并或跳跃获胜，倍增查找则白白浪费了它的探测。<bookmark mark='b'/>当一个列表长5倍或29倍时，倍增查找获胜，在 the AND whale 上快了将近8倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以搜索引擎按长度之比来选择，或者使用自适应算法，比如 Erik Demaine、Alejandro López-Ortiz 和 Ian Munro 的算法，它们在任何组合上都表现良好。而且比较次数并不是全部代价：第24部分的无分支循环，以及一次比较多个编号的 SIMD 指令，同样重要。

72f8802999a6.en: Some queries are phrases: white whale, the two words adjacent and in order. <bookmark mark='a'/> That is why our postings keep positions. First intersect the passage lists, as before. Then, inside each passage that has both words, shift every position of whale back by one, and intersect with the positions of white. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each survivor is a place where the phrase begins. <bookmark mark='c'/> In the novels, a hundred and twenty-five passages contain both white and whale, but only sixty-four contain the phrase. Three passages contain call, me and Ishmael, and exactly one has the phrase: the first line of chapter one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Positions are not free: four and a half million of them, beside two point four million passage ids. The next chapter makes all of it small.
72f8802999a6.zh: 有些查询是短语：white whale，两个词相邻且有序。<bookmark mark='a'/>这就是我们的倒排表保留位置的原因。先像之前那样求段落列表的交集。然后，在每个同时含有两个词的段落里，把 whale 的每个位置往回移一位，再与 white 的位置求交集。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个留下来的位置，都是这个短语开始的地方。<bookmark mark='c'/>在小说里，有125个段落同时含有 white 和 whale，但只有64个含有这个短语。有3个段落含有 call、me 和 Ishmael，而恰好只有一个含有这个短语：第一章的第一行。<bookmark mark='d'/>位置并不是免费的：一共有450万个，另外还有240万个段落编号。下一章把这一切都变小。

5a016b53f170.en: Chapter two's index holds two point three six million postings: as thirty-two-bit integers, nine and a half megabytes of document ids, and a web index holds vastly more. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are the first twelve passages that contain whale. <bookmark mark='b'/> The list is sorted, so store the differences between neighbours instead: the gaps. The first is the id plus one, since our codes start at one. <bookmark mark='c'/> A term in f of N passages has gaps averaging N over f: for whale, about twenty-nine. Frequent terms have short gaps; rare terms have long ones, but few. So give small numbers short codes.
5a016b53f170.zh: 第二章的索引有236万个倒排项：作为32位整数，光是文档编号就占9.5兆字节，而网络索引要多得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是包含 whale 的前12个段落。<bookmark mark='b'/>列表是有序的，所以改为存储相邻编号之差：间隔。第一个间隔是编号加1，因为我们的编码从1开始。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个出现在 N 个段落中 f 个里的词项，间隔平均为 N 除以 f：对 whale 来说大约是29。频繁的词项间隔短；罕见的词项间隔长，但数量少。所以给小的数短的编码。

613e96e01c01.en: The simplest code works in whole bytes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each byte carries seven bits of the gap and a flag that marks the last byte. <bookmark mark='b'/> One and five fit in a byte; six hundred and sixty has ten binary digits, so it takes two. <bookmark mark='c'/> Over the index: eight point six seven bits a posting, about a quarter of thirty-two. Decoding is a mask, a shift and a test, so it is fast. <bookmark mark='d'/> But a gap of one still costs eight bits.
613e96e01c01.zh: 最简单的编码以整字节为单位。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个字节携带间隔的7位，外加一个标记最后一个字节的标志位。<bookmark mark='b'/>1和5装得进一个字节；660有10位二进制数字，所以要两个字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>在整个索引上：每个倒排项8.67位，大约是32位的四分之一。解码只需一次掩码、一次移位和一次测试，所以很快。<bookmark mark='d'/>但间隔为1仍然要花8位。

fc48e66fe41a.en: Now we write bits. <bookmark mark='a'/> A gap g has floor of log two g, plus one, binary digits, the first always a one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Peter Elias's gamma code, from 1975, writes how many digits follow the first, as zeros, then the digits: twice floor log g, plus one, bits. Thirteen for a hundred. <bookmark mark='c'/> Part 1 of AI, Built showed that spending L bits on a value is ideal when its probability is two to the minus L. So gamma suits gaps that fall off like one over g squared. <bookmark mark='d'/> The delta code writes the digit count itself in gamma: eleven bits for a hundred. On our index, gamma spends five point six four bits a posting, and delta five point five four.
fc48e66fe41a.zh: 现在我们按位来写。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个间隔 g 有 log₂g 向下取整再加1位二进制数字，第一位总是1。<bookmark mark='b'/>Peter Elias 1975年的 γ 编码，先用若干个0写出第一位之后还有多少位，再写出这些数字：一共是 log g 向下取整的2倍再加1位。100要13位。<bookmark mark='c'/>《人工智能，从零搭建》第1部分说明过，当一个值的概率是2的负 L 次方时，为它花 L 位是最理想的。所以 γ 编码适合按 g 平方分之一衰减的间隔。<bookmark mark='d'/>δ 编码把位数本身用 γ 编码来写：100要11位。在我们的索引上，γ 编码每个倒排项花5.64位，δ 编码花5.54位。

71dffe9d0375.en: But we know each list's length, so fit the code to it. <bookmark mark='a'/> If each passage holds a term independently, with probability p equal to f over N, gaps are geometric. <bookmark mark='b'/> Solomon Golomb's code of 1966 divides g minus one by a parameter M: the quotient in unary, the remainder in binary. <bookmark mark='c'/> The quotient is geometric too, and unary, one more bit per step, is ideal when each step halves the probability. <bookmark mark='d'/> So set one minus p, to the power M, to one half: M is about point six nine times the mean gap, near twenty for whale. <bookmark mark='e'/> Rice rounds M down to a power of two, so the remainder takes exactly k bits: here, four.
71dffe9d0375.zh: 但我们知道每个列表的长度，所以可以让编码去适应它。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果每个段落都独立地包含一个词项，概率 p 等于 f 除以 N，那么间隔服从几何分布。<bookmark mark='b'/>Solomon Golomb 1966年的编码把 g 减1除以一个参数 M：商用一进制写，余数用二进制写。<bookmark mark='c'/>商也服从几何分布，而一进制每多一步就多一位，当每一步概率减半时它是最理想的。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以令1减 p 的 M 次方等于二分之一：M 大约是平均间隔的0.69倍，对 whale 来说接近20。<bookmark mark='e'/>Rice 编码把 M 向下取到2的幂，这样余数恰好占 k 位：这里是4位。

9d10b842d3d3.en: Here are Rice codes with k equal to two. <bookmark mark='a'/> Gaps of one to four take three bits, and each further four adds a single one. <bookmark mark='b'/> With its own k for every list, Rice spends four point nine six bits a posting over the whole index. <bookmark mark='c'/> And there is a floor. Choosing which f of N passages hold a term carries log of N choose f bits: four point seven four a posting here. Rice comes within five percent of it.
9d10b842d3d3.zh: 这是 k 等于2时的 Rice 编码。<bookmark mark='a'/>1到4的间隔占3位，此后每多4，就只多加一个1。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个列表用它自己的 k，Rice 编码在整个索引上每个倒排项花4.96位。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且存在一个下限。从 N 个段落中选出含有某个词项的 f 个，携带的信息是 N 选 f 的对数位：这里是每个倒排项4.74位。Rice 编码与它相差不到百分之五。

d42f61a4e280.en: Rice codes decode one bit at a time, through branches, so modern engines trade a few bits for speed. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a block of gaps and find the widest. <bookmark mark='b'/> Give every gap that many bits, packed side by side: no flags, no unary, no branches. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the SIMD instructions of Part 24 unpack four gaps at once. <bookmark mark='d'/> PForDelta, from 2006, stores the rare large gaps as exceptions, and Lemire and Boytsov's codecs of 2015 decode billions of integers a second.
d42f61a4e280.zh: Rice 编码要一位一位地解码，还要经过分支，所以现代搜索引擎多花几位来换取速度。<bookmark mark='a'/>取一块间隔，找出其中最宽的。<bookmark mark='b'/>让每个间隔都用那么多位，并排紧挨着打包：没有标志位，没有一进制，没有分支。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后第24部分的 SIMD 指令一次解包4个间隔。<bookmark mark='d'/>2006年的 PForDelta 把罕见的大间隔作为异常值另存，而 Lemire 和 Boytsov 2015年的编解码器每秒能解码数十亿个整数。

f31a373e26ba.en: Chapter five. From tf-idf to BM25.
f31a373e26ba.zh: 第五章：从 tf-idf 到 BM25。

809de73bb119.en: Boolean retrieval answers yes or no, but a reader wants the best passage first. <bookmark mark='a'/> A word that recurs in a passage says more about it, so weight it by its term frequency, damped by a logarithm: the tenth whale adds less than the first. <bookmark mark='b'/> And a rare word says more than a common one: Karen Spärck Jones, in 1972, weighted each term by the log of N over its document frequency. <bookmark mark='c'/> Whale, in three hundred and ninety of our passages, gets three point three six; Darcy, in a hundred and seventy-one, four point one nine.
809de73bb119.zh: 布尔检索只回答是或否，但读者想先看到最好的段落。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个词在一个段落里反复出现，就更能说明这个段落，所以按它的词频加权，并用对数加以抑制：第10个 whale 增加的分量少于第1个。<bookmark mark='b'/>而罕见的词比常见的词说明得更多：Karen Spärck Jones 在1972年用 N 除以文档频率的对数给每个词项加权。<bookmark mark='c'/>whale 出现在我们的390个段落里，权重是3.36；Darcy 出现在171个段落里，权重是4.19。

9ee7fd1098fe.en: Gerard Salton's SMART system made this geometry. <bookmark mark='a'/> A passage is a vector, one dimension per term, with these weights as coordinates; the query is a vector too. <bookmark mark='b'/> Rank passages by the cosine of the angle to the query: the dot product over both lengths. <bookmark mark='c'/> Dividing by length stops a long passage winning just by being long; our tf-idf divides by the square root of the length, a cheap stand-in. <bookmark mark='d'/> But why these weights? Nothing so far says.
9ee7fd1098fe.zh: Gerard Salton 的 SMART 系统把这变成了几何。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个段落是一个向量，每个词项一维，以这些权重为坐标；查询也是一个向量。<bookmark mark='b'/>按与查询夹角的余弦给段落排序：点积除以两者的长度。<bookmark mark='c'/>除以长度，可以避免一个长段落只因为长就胜出；我们的 tf-idf 除以长度的平方根，作为一个廉价的替代。<bookmark mark='d'/>但为什么是这些权重？到目前为止，什么都没有说明。

ffc4c5dbc5f6.en: In 1977 Stephen Robertson stated the principle that answers it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Rank documents by their probability of being relevant. <bookmark mark='b'/> If those probabilities are right, and documents are relevant independently, no other order puts more relevant documents, in expectation, into the top k, for any k. <bookmark mark='c'/> The proof is an exchange: swap a likelier document below the cut with a less likely one above it, and the expected count falls. <bookmark mark='d'/> So ranking reduces to estimating one probability from words.
ffc4c5dbc5f6.zh: 1977年，Stephen Robertson 陈述了回答这个问题的原理。<bookmark mark='a'/>按文档相关的概率给文档排序。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果这些概率是对的，并且各文档是否相关彼此独立，那么对任何 k，都没有别的顺序能让前 k 名中相关文档的期望数目更多。<bookmark mark='c'/>证明是一次交换：把截断线以下一个可能性更大的文档，与截断线以上一个可能性更小的文档对调，期望数目就会下降。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以排序归结为从词出发估计一个概率。

a4442aa250f6.en: The binary independence model is the simplest estimate. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ranking by probability is ranking by odds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Bayes' rule turns the odds around, and the prior odds are the same for every passage, so they drop out. <bookmark mark='c'/> Treat a passage as present or absent terms, independent given relevance. <bookmark mark='d'/> The log odds become a sum over the query terms the passage contains, each weighted by how much likelier it is in relevant passages. <bookmark mark='e'/> Knowing nothing about relevance, set p to one half; since almost every passage is irrelevant, set u to the document frequency over N. Out comes idf, derived rather than guessed: Robertson and Spärck Jones, 1976.
a4442aa250f6.zh: 二元独立模型是最简单的估计。<bookmark mark='a'/>按概率排序，就是按几率排序。<bookmark mark='b'/>贝叶斯法则把几率颠倒过来，而先验几率对每个段落都相同，所以可以消掉。<bookmark mark='c'/>把一个段落看作若干词项的出现或缺失，在给定相关性的条件下彼此独立。<bookmark mark='d'/>对数几率就变成对段落所含查询词项的求和，每一项的权重取决于它在相关段落中出现的可能性大多少。<bookmark mark='e'/>对相关性一无所知时，令 p 为二分之一；由于几乎每个段落都不相关，令 u 为文档频率除以 N。结果就得到 idf，是推导出来的，而不是猜出来的：Robertson 和 Spärck Jones，1976年。

5dce42386a93.en: But that model counts a word once, however often it appears, and a passage that says whale twenty times is likelier to be about whales. <bookmark mark='a'/> Stephen Harter's two-Poisson model of 1975 says a passage either is about the term or is not, with the count Poisson in each case; the weight it implies grows with the count and levels off. <bookmark mark='b'/> Robertson and Walker, in 1994, approximated it with one curve: term frequency times k one plus one, over term frequency plus k one. It is one at a single occurrence and rises towards k one plus one. <bookmark mark='c'/> With k one near zero, it is the binary model again; as k one grows, raw counts.
5dce42386a93.zh: 但这个模型对一个词只计一次，不管它出现多少次，而一个说了20次 whale 的段落，更可能是关于鲸的。<bookmark mark='a'/>Stephen Harter 1975年的双泊松模型认为，一个段落要么是关于这个词项的，要么不是，两种情况下计数都服从泊松分布；它所蕴含的权重随计数增长，然后趋于平稳。<bookmark mark='b'/>Robertson 和 Walker 在1994年用一条曲线来近似它：词频乘以 k1 加1，再除以词频加 k1。出现一次时它等于1，并逐渐上升，趋向 k1 加1。<bookmark mark='c'/>k1 接近0时，它又成了二元模型；随着 k1 增大，它就变成原始计数。

3efb518a4004.en: One more correction. <bookmark mark='a'/> A long passage repeats words because it is long, not because it is more about them. So BM25 scales k one by one minus b, plus b times the passage's length over the average. <bookmark mark='b'/> A passage twice the average needs more occurrences for the same weight; with b zero there is no normalization, with b one, full. <bookmark mark='c'/> Put together: idf from the binary model, saturation from two Poissons, and length. That is BM25, first run at TREC in 1994, and Lucene's default, with k one of one point two and b of three quarters.
3efb518a4004.zh: 再做一项修正。<bookmark mark='a'/>长段落重复一些词，是因为它长，而不是因为它更多地关于这些词。所以 BM25 把 k1 乘以1减 b、再加上 b 乘以段落长度与平均长度之比。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个两倍于平均长度的段落，需要出现更多次才能得到同样的权重；b 为0时没有归一化，b 为1时完全归一化。<bookmark mark='c'/>合在一起：来自二元模型的 idf，来自双泊松的饱和，以及长度。这就是 BM25，1994年在 TREC 上首次运行，也是 Lucene 的默认设置，k1 为1.2，b 为0.75。

7e7bb0145ef9.en: Chapter six. Is the ranking good?

fe6dd938c28b.en: To improve a ranking, we have to measure it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a ranking of ten passages, the relevant ones in colour. <bookmark mark='b'/> Precision at k is the fraction of the top k that is relevant: how much of what the reader sees is useful. <bookmark mark='c'/> Recall at k is the fraction of all relevant passages that the top k contains. Six exist here, and one is never retrieved. <bookmark mark='d'/> Reading further down, recall can only rise, while precision tends to fall, so one cutoff tells only part of the story.
fe6dd938c28b.zh: 要改进一个排序，就必须先测量它。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一个包含10个段落的排序，相关的段落用颜色标出。<bookmark mark='b'/>前 k 名的精确率，是前 k 名中相关段落所占的比例：读者看到的东西有多少是有用的。<bookmark mark='c'/>前 k 名的召回率，是全部相关段落中被前 k 名包含的比例。这里共有6个相关段落，其中一个始终没有被检索到。<bookmark mark='d'/>往下读得越远，召回率只会上升，而精确率往往下降，所以单个截断点只讲出了故事的一部分。

25f39d96cfc3.en: Average precision folds the list into one number. <bookmark mark='a'/> At each rank where a relevant passage appears, take the precision so far: one of one, two of three, three of four, and so on. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add them up and divide by the number of relevant passages, so the one never retrieved counts zero: here, point five nine. It rewards ranking relevant passages high and finding them all. <bookmark mark='c'/> Its mean over queries is MAP. On our nine test queries, cut at ten results, BM25 scores point eight zero and tf-idf point seven five.
25f39d96cfc3.zh: 平均精确率把这个列表折叠成一个数。<bookmark mark='a'/>在每个出现相关段落的排名上，取到那里为止的精确率：一分之一、三分之二、四分之三，依此类推。<bookmark mark='b'/>把它们加起来，除以相关段落的总数，所以那个从未被检索到的段落算作0：这里是0.59。它奖励把相关段落排得靠前，并且把它们全部找到。<bookmark mark='c'/>它在多个查询上的平均值就是 MAP。在我们的9个测试查询上，截取前10个结果，BM25 得0.80，tf-idf 得0.75。

52ddba04a669.en: But relevance comes in degrees, and readers rarely reach the bottom. Järvelin and Kekäläinen's measure of 2002 handles both. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each passage gets a grade, and a gain of two to the grade minus one, so a highly relevant passage is worth three relevant ones. <bookmark mark='b'/> Discount each gain by the log of its rank plus one: rank one counts in full, rank ten under a third. The sum is the discounted cumulative gain. <bookmark mark='c'/> Divide by the same sum for the ideal order of every judged passage, and each query scores between zero and one, however many relevant passages it has. Here, point eight zero.
52ddba04a669.zh: 但相关性是分等级的，而读者很少读到底部。Järvelin 和 Kekäläinen 2002年的度量同时处理了这两点。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个段落得到一个等级，以及2的等级次方减1的增益，所以一个高度相关的段落抵得上3个相关的段落。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个增益都按它的排名加1的对数打折扣：排名第1的完全计入，排名第10的不到三分之一。总和就是折损累计增益。<bookmark mark='c'/>再除以所有被评判过的段落按理想顺序排列时的同一个总和，每个查询的得分就落在0到1之间，不管它有多少相关段落。这里是0.80。

e15dd23ec36d.en: All of these need judgments. <bookmark mark='a'/> A test collection fixes documents, queries and judgments, so that systems are compared on equal terms, as Cyril Cleverdon's Cranfield experiments did in the 1960s. <bookmark mark='b'/> But nobody can judge every document for every query. Since 1992, NIST's Text Retrieval Conference has pooled the top hundred results of every submitted system, and assessors judge only the pool; anything unjudged counts as not relevant. <bookmark mark='c'/> Pools miss relevant documents, but Justin Zobel found in 1998 that comparisons between systems mostly survive. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our judgments are cruder: nine queries, each meant for one novel, graded by a rule rather than by people.
e15dd23ec36d.zh: 这些都需要相关性评判。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个测试集固定了文档、查询和评判，让各个系统在同等条件下比较，就像 Cyril Cleverdon 在20世纪60年代的 Cranfield 实验那样。<bookmark mark='b'/>但没有人能为每个查询评判每一篇文档。从1992年起，NIST 的文本检索会议（TREC）把每个提交系统的前100个结果汇集成一个池，评估员只评判这个池；任何没被评判的都算作不相关。<bookmark mark='c'/>池会漏掉相关文档，但 Justin Zobel 在1998年发现，系统之间的比较大多仍然成立。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的评判更粗糙：9个查询，每个针对一部小说，由一条规则而不是由人来分级。

829659735698.en: Here are our nine queries. <bookmark mark='a'/> For most, both rankers fill the top ten with relevant passages, and nDCG is one: names are easy. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sherlock Holmes scores point six zero for both, and the fault is ours. Four of the top ten come from The Hound of the Baskervilles, which has Holmes in it too, but our rule counts only the Adventures. A bad score can be a bad judgment. <bookmark mark='c'/> Vampire count is a real failure: The Count of Monte Cristo is full of the word count. <bookmark mark='d'/> On average, BM25 scores point eight five and tf-idf point eight three.
829659735698.zh: 这是我们的9个查询。<bookmark mark='a'/>对大多数查询，两种排序器都把前十名填满了相关段落，nDCG 为1：名字很容易。<bookmark mark='b'/>Sherlock Holmes 在两种排序器上都得0.60，而错在我们。前十名中有4个来自《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》（The Hound of the Baskervilles），里面也有 Holmes，但我们的规则只算《冒险史》（Adventures）。一个糟糕的分数，可能来自一次糟糕的评判。<bookmark mark='c'/>vampire count 是一次真正的失败：《基督山伯爵》（The Count of Monte Cristo）里满是 count 这个词。<bookmark mark='d'/>平均下来，BM25 得0.85，tf-idf 得0.83。

4895ff127468.en: Is that difference real, or luck? <bookmark mark='a'/> Pair the rankers query by query. Six queries tie, three favour BM25, and none favour tf-idf. <bookmark mark='b'/> If neither were better, each untied query would be a fair coin. <bookmark mark='c'/> Three heads in three tosses has probability one in eight, or one in four counting tails as well: p is point two five. Nine queries cannot tell. <bookmark mark='d'/> That is why TREC tracks use about fifty topics, with the paired tests and power calculations of Part 44; and in production, judged sets are joined by clicks and online experiments, which chapter twelve takes up.
4895ff127468.zh: 这个差别是真的，还是运气？<bookmark mark='a'/>按查询把两种排序器配成对。6个查询打平，3个偏向 BM25，没有一个偏向 tf-idf。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果两者都不更好，每个没打平的查询就像一次公平的抛硬币。<bookmark mark='c'/>抛3次全是正面的概率是八分之一，把全是反面也算上就是四分之一：p 等于0.25。9个查询分辨不出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是为什么 TREC 的评测任务用大约50个主题，并配合第44部分的配对检验和功效计算；而在生产中，评判过的数据集之外还要加上点击和在线实验，这是第十二章要讲的。

3d357fbb8dc7.zh: 第七章：快速求前 k 名。

aaf36d31fce0.en: A reader wants ten results, not a ranking of every passage. <bookmark mark='a'/> The simplest evaluation walks the postings of all the query's terms together, in document order, scores every passage containing any of them, and keeps the best ten in a min-heap. <bookmark mark='b'/> The smallest score in that heap is the threshold, theta: the score to beat. <bookmark mark='c'/> For the query the sea, eleven thousand two hundred and fifty-seven of our eleven thousand two hundred and sixty-one passages are scored, and all but ten scores are thrown away.
aaf36d31fce0.zh: 读者要的是10个结果，而不是每个段落的排序。<bookmark mark='a'/>最简单的求值方法按文档顺序一起遍历查询中所有词项的倒排表，给含有其中任何一个词的每个段落打分，并在一个最小堆里保留最好的10个。<bookmark mark='b'/>那个堆里最小的分数就是阈值 θ：要超过的分数。<bookmark mark='c'/>对查询 the sea，我们的11261个段落中有11257个被打分，而除了10个分数，其余全被丢掉。

a0c2acb6e123.en: Better to know, before scoring, the most a passage could score. <bookmark mark='a'/> When the index is built, store with each term the largest contribution it makes to any passage. Chapter five's saturation caps it anyway; the stored maximum is tighter. <bookmark mark='b'/> Suppose theta is two point six. A passage with only captain and ship scores at most two, so it cannot enter the top ten and need not be scored. <bookmark mark='c'/> Only passages with ahab can. Turtle and Flood's max-score, in 1995, used exactly this: terms whose bounds together cannot reach theta never propose a candidate.
a0c2acb6e123.zh: 最好能在打分之前，就知道一个段落最多能得多少分。<bookmark mark='a'/>建索引时，为每个词项存下它对任何段落所能做出的最大贡献。第五章的饱和本来就给它设了上限；存下的最大值更紧。<bookmark mark='b'/>假设 θ 是2.6。一个只含 captain 和 ship 的段落最多得2分，所以它进不了前十，也就不必打分。<bookmark mark='c'/>只有含 ahab 的段落才可能。Turtle 和 Flood 1995年的 max-score 正是这么做的：那些上界加起来也达不到 θ 的词项，永远不会提出候选。

3e882ce0f634.en: Broder and his colleagues, in 2003, made the bound into a walk called WAND, for weak, or weighted, and. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each term has a cursor. Sort the cursors by the document they point at, and add up their bounds in that order: the first cursor where the sum passes theta is the pivot. <bookmark mark='b'/> No earlier document can reach theta, so every earlier cursor jumps straight to the pivot document, with chapter three's skip pointers or galloping. <bookmark mark='c'/> When they all land on it, that document is scored in full. Here four of thirteen documents are scored: exactly those with ahab.
3e882ce0f634.zh: Broder 和同事在2003年把这个上界变成一种遍历，叫作 WAND，意思是弱的，或者说加权的 AND。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个词项有一个游标。按游标所指的文档给它们排序，再按这个顺序把它们的上界加起来：第一个使总和超过 θ 的游标就是枢轴。<bookmark mark='b'/>更早的文档都不可能达到 θ，所以每个更早的游标都直接跳到枢轴文档，用的是第三章的跳跃指针或倍增查找。<bookmark mark='c'/>当它们全都落在它上面时，这个文档才被完整地打分。这里13个文档中有4个被打分：恰好就是含有 ahab 的那些。

b1b58b99f66e.en: On the novels, with BM25 and a real, rising threshold, the savings are large. <bookmark mark='a'/> For white whale, WAND scores two hundred and thirty-five of the sixteen hundred and ten passages that contain a term. For the sea, about a tenth: the word the is everywhere, but its bound is tiny. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pride prejudice saves least: both words are rare, their bounds high, and nearly half the candidates must be checked. <bookmark mark='c'/> In every query the top ten is identical to exhaustive scoring, score for score. WAND is safe: it never trades accuracy for speed.
b1b58b99f66e.zh: 在小说上，用 BM25 和一个真实的、不断上升的阈值，节省是巨大的。<bookmark mark='a'/>对 white whale，在含有某个查询词项的1610个段落中，WAND 只给235个打分。对 the sea，大约十分之一：the 这个词无处不在，但它的上界很小。<bookmark mark='b'/>pride prejudice 节省最少：两个词都罕见，上界都高，将近一半的候选都必须检查。<bookmark mark='c'/>在每个查询中，前十名都与穷举打分完全相同，分数一分不差。WAND 是安全的：它从不拿准确性换速度。

551e853b634a.en: One maximum per term is loose: a single passage that says whale forty times sets the bound for the whole list. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ding and Suel, in 2011, stored a maximum for every block of postings, beside the skip data. <bookmark mark='b'/> After WAND picks a pivot, block-max WAND checks these tighter maxima, and skips whole blocks that cannot reach theta, without even decoding them. <bookmark mark='c'/> It is still safe. Lucene adopted it in 2019; since then Elasticsearch, by default, counts matches exactly only up to ten thousand, since counting all would mean visiting all.
551e853b634a.zh: 每个词项只存一个最大值是宽松的：一个说了40次 whale 的段落，就为整个列表定下了上界。<bookmark mark='a'/>Ding 和 Suel 在2011年为每一块倒排项都存了一个最大值，放在跳跃数据旁边。<bookmark mark='b'/>WAND 选出枢轴之后，块最大 WAND 检查这些更紧的最大值，并跳过达不到 θ 的整块，连解码都不用。<bookmark mark='c'/>它仍然是安全的。Lucene 在2019年采用了它；从那以后，Elasticsearch 默认只精确统计到1万个匹配，因为统计全部就意味着访问全部。

b7eb8811e1cb.en: Other shortcuts trade a little exactness for speed. <bookmark mark='a'/> A tiered index splits each term's postings: the highest-scoring in tier one, the rest in tier two. <bookmark mark='b'/> A query searches tier one, and goes on only if fewer than ten good answers came back. Champion lists, in Manning, Raghavan and Schütze's textbook, keep just each term's best few documents. <bookmark mark='c'/> These are unsafe: a passage strong only in the combination of its terms can be missed, and chapter six's metrics measure the loss. <bookmark mark='d'/> Tiers can also be ordered by a quality score for each page, such as one computed from links.
b7eb8811e1cb.zh: 其他捷径用一点精确性换取速度。<bookmark mark='a'/>分层索引把每个词项的倒排表拆开：得分最高的放在第一层，其余的放在第二层。<bookmark mark='b'/>查询先搜索第一层，只有在返回的好答案少于10个时才继续。Manning、Raghavan 和 Schütze 的教科书里的冠军列表，只保留每个词项最好的几个文档。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些都是不安全的：一个只在词项组合上才强的段落可能被漏掉，而第六章的指标能测出这种损失。<bookmark mark='d'/>各层也可以按每个网页的质量分数来排列，比如从链接计算出来的分数。

795dcc4f56ef.en: Chapter eight. Links and the random surfer.
795dcc4f56ef.zh: 第八章：链接与随机冲浪者。

d31f7d892317.en: Words say what a page is about, not whether it is any good. <bookmark mark='a'/> Sergey Brin and Larry Page, in 1998, read the links between pages as votes: a page is important if important pages link to it, and each page splits its vote among its links. <bookmark mark='b'/> The definition is circular, and a story resolves it. A surfer clicks a random link on every page, and now and then, bored, jumps to a random page. <bookmark mark='c'/> The fraction of time the surfer spends on each page, in the long run, is its PageRank. <bookmark mark='d'/> Brin and Page also indexed the text of each link as words describing its target.
d31f7d892317.zh: 词说明一个网页是关于什么的，而不说明它好不好。<bookmark mark='a'/>谢尔盖·布林和拉里·佩奇在1998年把网页之间的链接读作投票：如果重要的网页链接到一个网页，它就重要，而每个网页把自己的票分给它的各个链接。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个定义是循环的，一个故事解开了它。一个冲浪者在每个网页上点击一个随机链接，时不时地，他厌倦了，就跳到一个随机的网页。<bookmark mark='c'/>从长远看，冲浪者在每个网页上花的时间比例，就是它的 PageRank。<bookmark mark='d'/>布林和佩奇还把每个链接的文字作为描述其目标的词编入索引。

23c27eefa9e4.en: Write it down. <bookmark mark='a'/> With probability d the surfer follows a link; otherwise it teleports anywhere. So a page's rank is the teleport share, one minus d over the number of pages, plus d times the rank flowing in, each page giving an equal part of its rank to each of its links. Brin and Page suggested a d of zero point eight five. <bookmark mark='b'/> A page with no links passes its rank to everyone. <bookmark mark='c'/> In matrix form, the rank vector is the eigenvector of the Google matrix with eigenvalue one: the stationary distribution of a Markov chain, as in Part 18. <bookmark mark='d'/> Teleporting connects every page to every other, so by the Perron–Frobenius theorem that vector exists and is unique.
23c27eefa9e4.zh: 把它写下来。<bookmark mark='a'/>冲浪者以概率 d 跟随一个链接；否则就随机跳转到任何地方。所以一个网页的排名，是随机跳转的那一份，即1减 d 除以网页总数，加上 d 乘以流入的排名，每个网页把自己的排名平均分给它的每个链接。布林和佩奇建议 d 取0.85。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个没有链接的网页，把它的排名传给所有网页。<bookmark mark='c'/>写成矩阵形式，排名向量就是 Google 矩阵对应特征值1的特征向量：一条马尔可夫链的平稳分布，就像第18部分那样。<bookmark mark='d'/>随机跳转让每个网页都连到其他每个网页，所以根据 Perron–Frobenius 定理，这个向量存在而且唯一。

f0145d140741.en: To compute it, start from the uniform vector and multiply by the matrix, again and again. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our synthetic web has four hundred pages, each linking to up to four earlier ones, chosen in proportion to the links they already have, plus a farm of twenty. <bookmark mark='b'/> At each step the change shrinks by at least a factor d, and here faster: to one part in a million after forty steps. The bound does not depend on the number of pages, so a web of billions also needs only a few dozen passes. <bookmark mark='c'/> The top pages are the oldest, which preferential attachment made into hubs.
f0145d140741.zh: 要计算它，从均匀向量出发，一遍又一遍地乘以这个矩阵。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的合成网络有400个网页，每个链接到至多4个更早的网页，按它们已有的链接数成比例地选，另外还有一个由20个网页组成的链接农场。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一步，变化至少缩小为原来的 d 倍，而这里更快：40步之后缩小到百万分之一。这个界不依赖网页的数目，所以几十亿个网页的网络也只需要几十遍。<bookmark mark='c'/>排名最高的网页是最老的那些，优先连接让它们成了枢纽。

4833f4028665.en: Jon Kleinberg, at the same time, read links differently. <bookmark mark='a'/> Authorities are pages linked to by good hubs; hubs are pages that link to good authorities. Each score is the sum of the other kind over the links. <bookmark mark='b'/> Iterate and normalise, and the two vectors converge to the leading eigenvectors of A transpose A and A A transpose, the singular vectors of the link matrix. Kleinberg ran it on the neighbourhood of a query's results. <bookmark mark='c'/> On our web it is easily led. The top authority is the farm's target, the top hub is a farm page, and all twenty farm pages are among the twenty best hubs.
4833f4028665.zh: 与此同时，Jon Kleinberg 用另一种方式解读链接。<bookmark mark='a'/>权威是被好的枢纽链接的网页；枢纽是链接到好的权威的网页。每个分数都是另一种分数沿链接的总和。<bookmark mark='b'/>反复迭代并归一化，两个向量就收敛到 A 转置 A 和 A A 转置的主特征向量，也就是链接矩阵的奇异向量。Kleinberg 在一个查询结果的邻域上运行它。<bookmark mark='c'/>在我们的网络上，它很容易被带偏。排名第一的权威是农场的目标，排名第一的枢纽是一个农场网页，而全部20个农场网页都在最好的20个枢纽之中。

864c41021ec9.en: That farm is link spam: twenty pages linking to one target and to one another. <bookmark mark='a'/> Without it, the target, the newest page of our web, ranks three hundred and forty-sixth of four hundred. <bookmark mark='b'/> With it, a hundred and fourteenth of four hundred and twenty: each farm page collects its teleport share and passes most of it on. <bookmark mark='c'/> Defences followed. In 2005 the major search engines agreed on a nofollow attribute, for links a site does not vouch for, such as those in comments. TrustRank, from Gyöngyi, Garcia-Molina and Pedersen in 2004, teleports only to pages people have checked. Today links are one signal among many, combined by learned rankers, as chapter twelve will show.
864c41021ec9.zh: 那个农场就是链接作弊：20个网页链接到同一个目标，也互相链接。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有它，这个目标，也就是我们网络中最新的网页，在400个网页中排第346。<bookmark mark='b'/>有了它，在420个网页中排第114：每个农场网页收下它那份随机跳转的排名，再把大部分传出去。<bookmark mark='c'/>防御随之而来。2005年，各大搜索引擎就一个 nofollow 属性达成一致，用于网站不为之担保的链接，比如评论里的链接。TrustRank 由 Gyöngyi、Garcia-Molina 和 Pedersen 在2004年提出，它只随机跳转到经过人工核查的网页。今天，链接只是许多信号中的一个，由学习得到的排序器组合起来，第十二章会展示这一点。

7868a4437bf9.en: Before anything can be indexed, it must be fetched. <bookmark mark='a'/> A crawler starts from seed addresses in a frontier. It takes one, looks up the host, checks the site's robots dot t x t, downloads the page and parses it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each link found is normalised, so that one page has one address, and tested against the addresses already seen, a hash set of fingerprints as in Part 17. New ones join the frontier. <bookmark mark='c'/> The text is fingerprinted too, so copies are not indexed twice. Heydon and Najork's Mercator set this design out in 1999. Crawlers must also escape traps, like a calendar linking to the next day, forever.
7868a4437bf9.zh: 任何东西在被索引之前，都必须先被抓取。<bookmark mark='a'/>爬虫从待抓取队列（frontier）里的种子地址出发。它取出一个地址，查找主机，检查网站的 robots.txt，下载网页并解析它。<bookmark mark='b'/>找到的每个链接都要规范化，让一个网页只有一个地址，再与已经见过的地址比对，那是第17部分那样的一个指纹哈希集合。新的地址加入待抓取队列。<bookmark mark='c'/>文本也要算指纹，这样副本就不会被索引两次。Heydon 和 Najork 的 Mercator 在1999年阐述了这种设计。爬虫还必须逃离陷阱，比如一个日历永远链接到下一天。

6578e34420d0.en: The frontier decides what to fetch next, and it serves two masters. <bookmark mark='a'/> Priority: important and fast-changing pages first, held in Mercator's front queues. <bookmark mark='b'/> And politeness: never hammer one server. Back queues hold one host each, and a heap records when each host may next be contacted. A common rule, in Manning, Raghavan and Schütze's textbook, waits about ten times as long as the last fetch from that host took. <bookmark mark='c'/> Sites also state their wishes. Martijn Koster's robots exclusion convention of 1994 lists paths a crawler should leave alone; in 2022 it became an internet standard, RFC nine three oh nine. A polite crawler fetches from thousands of hosts at once, and from each one slowly.
6578e34420d0.zh: 待抓取队列决定下一个抓取什么，它要同时满足两个要求。<bookmark mark='a'/>优先级：重要的、变化快的网页先抓，放在 Mercator 的前端队列里。<bookmark mark='b'/>还有礼貌：绝不猛击同一台服务器。每个后端队列只放一个主机，一个堆记录每个主机下一次可以联系的时间。Manning、Raghavan 和 Schütze 的教科书里有一条常用规则：等待的时间大约是上一次从那个主机抓取所用时间的10倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>网站也会声明自己的意愿。Martijn Koster 1994年的 robots 排除约定，列出爬虫不应触碰的路径；2022年它成为一项互联网标准，RFC 9309。一个有礼貌的爬虫同时从成千上万个主机抓取，而对每一个都慢慢地抓。

8b7b42a3c901.en: The web changes after it is crawled, so a crawler must come back. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are two pages, one changing often and one rarely, revisited at the same rate. Between a change and the next visit, our copy is stale. <bookmark mark='b'/> If a page changes at random at a rate lambda, and we revisit every interval I, our copy is fresh for a fraction one minus e to the minus lambda I, over lambda I, of the time. <bookmark mark='c'/> Junghoo Cho and Hector Garcia-Molina found a surprise in 2000. With a fixed budget, revisiting every page equally often beats revisiting in proportion to change, and the best policy visits the fastest-changing pages less, since their copies go stale almost at once.
8b7b42a3c901.zh: 网页被爬取之后还会变化，所以爬虫必须回来。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是两个网页，一个经常变化，一个很少变化，以同样的频率重访。在一次变化和下一次访问之间，我们的副本是过时的。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果一个网页以速率 λ 随机变化，而我们每隔时间 I 重访一次，那么我们的副本保持新鲜的时间比例是：1减 e 的负 λI 次方，再除以 λI。<bookmark mark='c'/>Junghoo Cho 和 Hector Garcia-Molina 在2000年发现了一个出人意料的结果。在预算固定时，以同样的频率重访每个网页，胜过按变化频率成比例地重访；而最好的策略对变化最快的网页反而访问得更少，因为它们的副本几乎立刻就过时了。

2290b5ab42dc.en: Much of the web is copied: mirrors, syndicated articles, pages that differ only in an advertisement. <bookmark mark='a'/> Moses Charikar's SimHash, of 2002, makes a fingerprint that changes a little when the text does. Cut the text into overlapping three-word shingles, and hash each one to sixty-four bits. <bookmark mark='b'/> For each bit position, add one for every shingle with a one there, and subtract one for every zero. <bookmark mark='c'/> The fingerprint keeps the signs. A small edit changes a few shingles, which rarely flips a sign. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is Part 20's random-hyperplane sketch: each bit says on which side of a random hyperplane the document's vector of shingles lies.
2290b5ab42dc.zh: 网络上很多内容是复制的：镜像、转载的文章、只差一条广告的网页。<bookmark mark='a'/>Moses Charikar 2002年的 SimHash 生成一种指纹，文本稍有变化，它也只变化一点。把文本切成相互重叠的三词瓦片，把每个瓦片哈希成64位。<bookmark mark='b'/>对每个位的位置，凡是这一位为1的瓦片就加1，为0的就减1。<bookmark mark='c'/>指纹保留这些和的符号。一个小的修改只改变几个瓦片，很少会翻转一个符号。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是第20部分的随机超平面草图：每一位说明文档的瓦片向量位于一个随机超平面的哪一侧。

185ace79c76d.en: How well does it work on the novels? <bookmark mark='a'/> We fingerprinted two hundred passages and replaced words at random. One replaced word moves two point four bits on average; eighty words, a fifth of the passage, about twenty. Unrelated passages differ in about thirty-two bits, half of sixty-four, and the closest unrelated pair in twenty-two. <bookmark mark='b'/> Manku, Jain and Das Sarma, at Google in 2007, found three bits a good threshold for eight billion pages. To search quickly, cut the fingerprints into four blocks of sixteen bits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Three differing bits spoil at most three blocks, so one block agrees exactly, and an exact lookup per block, in four sorted tables, finds every candidate.
185ace79c76d.zh: 它在小说上效果如何？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们给200个段落算了指纹，并随机替换其中的词。替换一个词，平均让2.4位改变；替换80个词，也就是段落的五分之一，大约改变20位。不相关的段落相差大约32位，即64的一半，而最接近的一对不相关段落相差22位。<bookmark mark='b'/>Manku、Jain 和 Das Sarma 2007年在 Google 发现，对80亿个网页来说，3位是一个好的阈值。为了快速搜索，把指纹切成4块，每块16位。<bookmark mark='c'/>3个不同的位至多破坏3块，所以总有一块完全一致，而在4张有序表里对每块做一次精确查找，就能找到所有候选。

721364e57e02.en: One machine cannot hold the web's index, or answer the world's queries, so the index must be cut into pieces. <bookmark mark='a'/> Picture it as a matrix: a row for each term, a column for each passage, a dot for each posting. Ours has 40,692 rows and 11,261 columns, and it is almost empty. <bookmark mark='b'/> Cut it by columns and each shard is a complete little index for a slice of the passages: document partitioning. <bookmark mark='c'/> Cut it by rows and each server holds the whole postings list of some terms: term partitioning. The matrix is the same; what differs is the work a query causes.
721364e57e02.zh: 一台机器既装不下整个网络的索引，也回答不了全世界的查询，所以索引必须被切成若干块。<bookmark mark='a'/>把它想象成一个矩阵：每个词项一行，每个段落一列，每个倒排项一个点。我们的矩阵有40692行、11261列，而且几乎是空的。<bookmark mark='b'/>按列切，每个分片就是一部分段落的一个完整的小索引：按文档划分。<bookmark mark='c'/>按行切，每台服务器保存某些词项的完整倒排表：按词项划分。矩阵是同一个；不同的是一次查询引起的工作。

ee4aa07c5e6b.en: Follow the query whale sea through each layout. <bookmark mark='a'/> With documents partitioned, the broker sends the whole query to every shard. Each computes its own top ten over its quarter of the passages, and the broker merges four short lists. The scores need collection-wide statistics, such as idf, shared among the shards. <bookmark mark='b'/> With terms partitioned, only the two servers holding those terms work, but one must ship its entire list, 390 postings, to the other, which intersects them and finds 231 passages. <bookmark mark='c'/> Web engines chose documents: Google's cluster, described by Barroso, Dean and Hoelzle in 2003, cut its index into shards of documents.
ee4aa07c5e6b.zh: 顺着查询 whale sea 走一遍这两种布局。<bookmark mark='a'/>按文档划分时，代理（broker）把整个查询发给每个分片。每个分片在自己那四分之一的段落上算出自己的前十名，代理再合并4个短列表。打分需要整个文档集合的统计量，比如 idf，在各分片之间共享。<bookmark mark='b'/>按词项划分时，只有保存这两个词项的两台服务器工作，但其中一台必须把它的整个列表，390个倒排项，发给另一台，由后者求交集，找出231个段落。<bookmark mark='c'/>网络搜索引擎选择了按文档划分：Barroso、Dean 和 Hoelzle 在2003年描述的 Google 集群，把它的索引切成了由文档组成的分片。

f77d52430e13.en: Document partitioning has a price, which Part 39 called the tail at scale. <bookmark mark='a'/> A query waits for its slowest shard. Suppose, as Dean and Barroso did in 2013, that each server is slow on one request in a hundred. A query that touches one server is slow one time in a hundred; a query that must wait for a hundred servers is slow sixty-three times in a hundred. <bookmark mark='b'/> One remedy is the hedged request: after a short delay, send a second copy to another replica and keep whichever answers first. In their test it cut the ninety-nine point nine percentile from one thousand eight hundred milliseconds to seventy-four, for two percent more requests. <bookmark mark='c'/> Another is to answer without the stragglers.
f77d52430e13.zh: 按文档划分有一个代价，第39部分称之为规模下的尾部。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个查询要等它最慢的分片。假设像 Dean 和 Barroso 在2013年那样，每台服务器每100个请求中有一个很慢。只涉及一台服务器的查询，每100次中慢1次；必须等100台服务器的查询，每100次中慢63次。<bookmark mark='b'/>一种补救办法是对冲请求：在一小段延迟之后，把同一个请求再发一份给另一个副本，谁先回答就用谁。在他们的测试中，它把第99.9百分位数从1800毫秒降到74毫秒，只多了百分之二的请求。<bookmark mark='c'/>另一种办法是不等掉队者就作答。

4921e3476bbc.en: A real deployment is a grid. <bookmark mark='a'/> The columns are shards, each holding a slice of the index; the rows are replicas, identical copies. A query visits one replica of every shard, chosen by load. <bookmark mark='b'/> When a machine fails, as one in a big cluster always is, the broker sends that shard's work to another copy, and the user notices nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> The grid grows in two directions. More queries per second? Add a row of replicas. <bookmark mark='d'/> A bigger index? Add a column of shards, each smaller, so each answers faster. Capacity and size are separate dials.
4921e3476bbc.zh: 真实的部署是一张网格。<bookmark mark='a'/>列是分片，每个保存索引的一部分；行是副本，完全相同的拷贝。一个查询访问每个分片的一个副本，按负载来选。<bookmark mark='b'/>当一台机器出故障时，而在一个大集群里总有一台是坏的，代理就把那个分片的工作发给另一份拷贝，用户什么也察觉不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>这张网格朝两个方向增长。每秒查询更多？加一行副本。<bookmark mark='d'/>索引更大？加一列分片，每个分片更小，所以每个都回答得更快。容量和规模是两个独立的旋钮。

759a7855e48d.en: The cheapest query is one you have already answered. <bookmark mark='a'/> Queries are skewed the way words are: as Chapter 1 found for the novels, a few are enormously common and most are rare, so a small head of popular queries recurs all day. <bookmark mark='b'/> A result cache in front of the broker stores whole answer pages for that head. A hit goes straight back without touching a shard. Entries must expire, because the index keeps changing underneath them. <bookmark mark='c'/> A miss takes the full path, and that is where the tail lives. Inside each shard a second cache keeps the postings of popular terms in memory. Baeza-Yates and colleagues showed in 2007 that the best terms to keep are those queries use often relative to the length of their lists.
759a7855e48d.zh: 最便宜的查询是你已经回答过的查询。<bookmark mark='a'/>查询的偏斜和词一样：正如第一章在小说上发现的，少数查询极其常见，大多数很罕见，所以一小撮热门查询整天反复出现。<bookmark mark='b'/>代理前面的结果缓存，为这一小撮查询保存整页答案。命中的请求不碰任何分片就直接返回。缓存条目必须过期，因为它们底下的索引一直在变。<bookmark mark='c'/>未命中的请求走完整条路径，而尾部就在那里。在每个分片内部，第二个缓存把热门词项的倒排表保留在内存里。Baeza-Yates 和同事在2007年证明，最值得保留的词项，是那些被查询使用的频率相对于其列表长度较高的词项。

69731046cdf7.zh: 第十一章：拼写纠错与自动补全。

00c5d2e27434.en: A user types c a p t i a n. What did they mean? <bookmark mark='a'/> Model the error as a message sent through a noisy channel: the intended word goes in, the fingers garble it, and a typo comes out. Here two letters were swapped. <bookmark mark='b'/> To decode, pick the word maximizing its prior probability times the probability that the channel turned it into this typo. <bookmark mark='c'/> The prior is a language model; ours is simply each word's count in the novels. The channel model says which slips are likely; ours charges a fixed penalty per edit. Kernighan, Church and Gale learned it instead, from real typing errors, in 1990. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is Bayes' rule.
00c5d2e27434.zh: 一位用户输入了 c a p t i a n。他想输入的是什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>把这个错误建模为一条经过噪声信道发送的消息：想要的词进去，手指把它弄乱，出来一个拼写错误。这里有两个字母被对调了。<bookmark mark='b'/>要解码，就选出那个使先验概率乘以“信道把它变成这个错误的概率”达到最大的词。<bookmark mark='c'/>先验是一个语言模型；我们的先验只是每个词在小说里的计数。信道模型说明哪些失误是常见的；我们的信道模型对每次编辑收取固定的罚分。Kernighan、Church 和 Gale 在1990年则从真实的打字错误中把它学了出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是贝叶斯法则。

8bee2484bb3d.en: The channel needs a distance between a typo and a word. <bookmark mark='a'/> It is the edit distance of Part 21: the fewest insertions, deletions and substitutions turning one string into the other. <bookmark mark='b'/> Lay one word across the top and the other down the side. Each cell is the cheapest of its three neighbours plus one, or its diagonal neighbour for free when the letters agree. That is the dynamic programming of Part 19, filled row by row. <bookmark mark='c'/> The corner says 2: a single swap of neighbouring letters costs two substitutions. Damerau observed in 1964 that transposing two neighbours is among the commonest slips, and counted it as one edit.
8bee2484bb3d.zh: 信道需要一个拼写错误与一个词之间的距离。<bookmark mark='a'/>这就是第21部分的编辑距离：把一个字符串变成另一个所需的最少插入、删除和替换次数。<bookmark mark='b'/>把一个词横放在顶上，另一个竖放在侧边。每个格子取它三个邻居中最便宜的那个再加1，或者在字母相同时免费取它的对角邻居。这就是第19部分的动态规划，一行一行地填。<bookmark mark='c'/>角上的格子是2：对调一对相邻字母要花两次替换。Damerau 在1964年观察到，对调两个相邻字母是最常见的失误之一，于是把它算作一次编辑。

1c22779c5205.en: Comparing a typo with every word in the vocabulary is wasteful. Burkhard and Keller's tree of 1973 does better. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each word hangs below its parent on an edge labelled with the edit distance between them. <bookmark mark='b'/> To find words within one edit of a typo, compute its distance d to the root. Because edit distance is a metric, the triangle inequality says that a match can only lie under the edges labelled d minus one to d plus one, and every other subtree is skipped unvisited. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the novels' vocabulary, at a tolerance of two, our tree still computes about a third of all the distances: pruning is weak when the tolerance is large compared with the words themselves.
1c22779c5205.zh: 把一个拼写错误与词汇表中的每个词比较是浪费。Burkhard 和 Keller 1973年的树做得更好。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个词挂在它的父节点下面，连接它们的边标着两者之间的编辑距离。<bookmark mark='b'/>要找出与一个拼写错误相差一次编辑以内的词，先算出它到根的距离 d。因为编辑距离是一种度量，三角不等式表明，匹配只可能位于标着 d 减1到 d 加1的那些边下面，其他每棵子树都不用访问就跳过。<bookmark mark='c'/>在小说的词汇表上，容差为2时，我们的树仍要计算全部距离的大约三分之一：当容差相对于词本身较大时，剪枝的效果很弱。

aa3306dbd07a.en: Here is the whole corrector on seven inputs, with a vocabulary of 31,190 words from the novels. <bookmark mark='a'/> Misspelt captain, Elizabeth, separate, monster and London are all repaired. <bookmark mark='b'/> Whale is already a word: it has 76 neighbours within two edits, but none is common enough to pay for the change, so it stays. <bookmark mark='c'/> And one is wrong. Recieve becomes relieve, because relieve is one substitution away while receive, under plain edit distance, is two. Damerau's transposition, or a channel learned from real slips, would put it right. <bookmark mark='d'/> Real correctors also read the surrounding words, and learn from query logs what people retyped next.
aa3306dbd07a.zh: 这是整个纠错器在7个输入上的表现，词汇表取自小说，共31190个词。<bookmark mark='a'/>拼错的 captain、Elizabeth、separate、monster 和 London 都被修复了。<bookmark mark='b'/>Whale 本身已经是一个词：它在两次编辑以内有76个邻居，但没有一个常见到值得做这次改动，所以它保持不变。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有一个改错了。recieve 变成了 relieve，因为 relieve 只差一次替换，而 receive 在普通的编辑距离下差两次。Damerau 的换位，或者从真实失误中学出的信道，就能把它改对。<bookmark mark='d'/>真实的纠错器还会读周围的词，并从查询日志中学习人们接下来重新输入了什么。

20f509da8d1b.en: Better still is to catch the query before it is finished. <bookmark mark='a'/> Autocompletion is a walk down a trie, the tree of prefixes from Part 17. Type c, a, and every word below that node is a candidate. <bookmark mark='b'/> The best five, ranked by their counts in the novels, are can, came, called, cannot and can't. <bookmark mark='c'/> To find them without visiting the whole subtree, store at every node the best count anywhere beneath it. A priority queue then always expands the most promising node, and the top k come out after about k times the depth steps, however big the vocabulary. <bookmark mark='d'/> Or store the top few at each node outright, buying speed with memory. Real engines rank completions by what people search for.
20f509da8d1b.zh: 更好的做法是在查询输完之前就把它截住。<bookmark mark='a'/>自动补全是沿着一棵字典树往下走，也就是第17部分的前缀树。输入 c、a，那个节点下面的每个词都是候选。<bookmark mark='b'/>按在小说中的计数排序，最好的5个是 can、came、called、cannot 和 can't。<bookmark mark='c'/>要在不访问整棵子树的情况下找到它们，就在每个节点存下它下面任何地方的最大计数。然后一个优先队列总是展开最有希望的节点，前 k 名大约在 k 乘以深度那么多步之后就出来，不管词汇表有多大。<bookmark mark='d'/>或者干脆在每个节点直接存下前几名，用内存换速度。真实的搜索引擎按人们搜索什么来给补全排序。

695a2d5ac2d7.en: BM25 is one signal. A web engine has hundreds. <bookmark mark='a'/> For each query and passage it computes a vector of features: BM25 and tf-idf, whether the phrase occurs, how close the terms sit, the length, and on the web PageRank and the clicks of past users. <bookmark mark='b'/> Hand-tuning a formula that weighs a hundred of these is hopeless, so a model learns it from graded queries, like our 9 from Chapter 6, but thousands of them, graded by people. Microsoft's public MSLR data set describes each query and page by a hundred and thirty-six features. <bookmark mark='c'/> The model outputs a score to sort by. The real question is what loss to train it on.
695a2d5ac2d7.zh: BM25 只是一个信号。网络搜索引擎有几百个。<bookmark mark='a'/>对每个查询和段落，它计算一个特征向量：BM25 和 tf-idf，短语是否出现，词项挨得多近，长度，在网络上还有 PageRank 和以往用户的点击。<bookmark mark='b'/>手工调一个给上百个这样的特征加权的公式是没有希望的，所以由一个模型从分过级的查询中学习它，就像我们第六章的9个查询，但要成千上万个，由人来分级。微软公开的 MSLR 数据集用136个特征描述每个查询和网页。<bookmark mark='c'/>模型输出一个用来排序的分数。真正的问题是用什么损失来训练它。

0f256e6633f3.en: There are three families of loss. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pointwise methods predict each passage's grade by regression, one at a time. But the user only ever sees an order, and grades are not comparable across queries. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pairwise methods look at pairs: whenever one passage is better than another, it should score higher. Burges and colleagues' RankNet, in 2005, used a logistic loss on the difference of the two scores. But it counts every misordered pair the same, whether at the top of the page or far below it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Listwise methods judge the whole list by the measure we care about, such as nDCG. But nDCG only changes when two scores cross, so it has no useful gradient.
0f256e6633f3.zh: 损失有三大类。<bookmark mark='a'/>逐点方法用回归预测每个段落的等级，一次一个。但用户看到的只是一个顺序，而且不同查询之间的等级无法比较。<bookmark mark='b'/>成对方法看的是段落对：只要一个段落比另一个好，它的分数就应该更高。Burges 和同事2005年的 RankNet，对两个分数之差使用逻辑斯谛损失。但它对每一对排错的段落一视同仁，不管是在页面顶部，还是在远远的下方。<bookmark mark='c'/>列表方法用我们关心的度量，比如 nDCG，来评判整个列表。但 nDCG 只在两个分数交叉时才变化，所以它没有有用的梯度。

f43ee9d7245e.en: Burges and colleagues found a way round that in 2006. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take six graded passages, in the model's current order. <bookmark mark='b'/> RankNet's gradient pushes each passage up for every worse passage above it, and down for every better one below, by an amount that depends only on the two scores. <bookmark mark='c'/> LambdaRank multiplies each pair's push by how much nDCG would change if the two swapped places. Pairs near the top now dominate, and pairs low on the page barely count. <bookmark mark='d'/> The trick is to never write a loss down at all: define the gradient you want, the lambdas, and follow it. Passage C, the best, gets the strongest push.
f43ee9d7245e.zh: Burges 和同事在2006年找到了绕过它的办法。<bookmark mark='a'/>取6个分过级的段落，按模型当前的顺序排列。<bookmark mark='b'/>RankNet 的梯度，每有一个更差的段落排在它上面，就把它往上推，每有一个更好的段落排在它下面，就把它往下推，推动的幅度只取决于两个分数。<bookmark mark='c'/>LambdaRank 把每一对的推力，乘以两者交换位置时 nDCG 会改变多少。现在靠近顶部的对占主导，而页面下方的对几乎不算数。<bookmark mark='d'/>诀窍在于根本不写出损失：定义你想要的梯度，也就是那些 lambda，然后跟着它走。段落 C 最好，得到最强的推力。

831f2f0e8d3f.en: Lambdas are gradients, and AI, Built Part 6 showed what to do with gradients over tabular features: boost trees. <bookmark mark='a'/> LambdaMART starts from some scores, computes every passage's lambda, and fits a small regression tree that predicts them from the features, added with a small weight. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the lambdas are recomputed, and another tree fits them. In our picture nDCG climbs from 0.60 to 0.94, and then to one, the ideal order. <bookmark mark='c'/> Because trees split on features, the model generalizes to queries it never saw. An ensemble built on these lambda gradients won Yahoo's Learning to Rank Challenge in 2010, and LightGBM and XGBoost offer it as a standard objective.
831f2f0e8d3f.zh: lambda 就是梯度，而《人工智能，从零搭建》第6部分已经说明了，对表格特征上的梯度该怎么做：提升树。<bookmark mark='a'/>LambdaMART 从某些分数出发，算出每个段落的 lambda，并拟合一棵小的回归树，用特征来预测它们，再以一个小的权重加上去。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后重新计算 lambda，再用另一棵树拟合它们。在我们的图中，nDCG 从0.60升到0.94，然后升到1，也就是理想的顺序。<bookmark mark='c'/>因为树是按特征分裂的，模型能推广到它从未见过的查询。一个建立在这些 lambda 梯度上的集成模型，赢得了2010年 Yahoo 的排序学习挑战赛，而 LightGBM 和 XGBoost 把它作为一个标准的目标函数提供。

184563e48810.en: Judged queries are expensive; clicks are free, but biased. <bookmark mark='a'/> People mostly look at the top of the page, so a click depends on where a result was shown as well as on whether it was relevant. <bookmark mark='b'/> Joachims and colleagues showed this in 2005 with eye tracking: when the top two results were secretly swapped, users still clicked the first more often. <bookmark mark='c'/> In the cascade model of Craswell and colleagues, the user reads down the page and clicks the first result that looks right. <bookmark mark='d'/> To learn from clicks without learning the old ranking back, weight each click by one over the chance its position was looked at, measured by randomly swapping results: unbiased learning to rank.
184563e48810.zh: 评判过的查询很昂贵；点击是免费的，但有偏差。<bookmark mark='a'/>人们大多只看页面的顶部，所以一次点击既取决于结果显示在哪里，也取决于它是否相关。<bookmark mark='b'/>Joachims 和同事在2005年用眼动追踪证明了这一点：当前两个结果被悄悄对调时，用户仍然更常点击第一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>在 Craswell 和同事的级联模型中，用户沿着页面往下读，点击第一个看起来合适的结果。<bookmark mark='d'/>要从点击中学习，又不把旧的排序学回来，就给每次点击乘以“它的位置被看到的概率”的倒数，这个概率通过随机对调结果来测量：这就是无偏排序学习。

91aa2b4d5a3f.en: Everything so far matches words. <bookmark mark='a'/> A query about a voyage on the ocean scores zero against a passage about a ship at sea, because they share no terms. <bookmark mark='b'/> Dense retrieval moves the problem into geometry. An encoder, the embeddings of AI, Built Part 24, maps every passage to a vector, once, offline, and the query at query time; relevance is a dot product. <bookmark mark='c'/> Related passages land near each other, and retrieval becomes nearest-neighbour search. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our own vectors are a stand-in: tf-idf projected down to 64 dimensions by a random matrix, the trick of Part 20. They keep the geometry of words, not of meaning; a trained encoder, like the dense passage retriever of Karpukhin and colleagues in 2020, learns meaning from examples.
91aa2b4d5a3f.zh: 到目前为止，一切都是在匹配词。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个关于在大洋上航行的查询，与一个关于海上一艘船的段落得分为0，因为它们没有共同的词项。<bookmark mark='b'/>稠密检索把这个问题搬进几何。一个编码器，也就是《人工智能，从零搭建》第24部分的嵌入，把每个段落映射成一个向量，只做一次，离线完成，而查询在查询时才映射；相关性就是一个点积。<bookmark mark='c'/>相关的段落落在彼此附近，检索就变成了最近邻搜索。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们自己的向量只是一个替代品：tf-idf 由一个随机矩阵投影到64维，这是第20部分的技巧。它们保留的是词的几何，而不是意思的几何；一个训练过的编码器，比如 Karpukhin 和同事2020年的稠密段落检索器，从例子中学习意思。

0eb4f66283da.en: A float vector per passage costs 256 bytes; a billion passages would need hundreds of gigabytes. Jegou, Douze and Schmid's product quantization, of 2011, shrinks it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cut each vector into 8 pieces of 8 dimensions. <bookmark mark='b'/> In each piece's space, cluster all passages into two hundred and fifty-six groups, and store only the number of the nearest centre: one byte. The vector becomes 8 bytes. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two hundred and fifty-six choices in each of eight places give an astronomical number of codes, from very few centres. <bookmark mark='d'/> Searching needs no decompression: compute the query's distance to every centre once, and each passage's distance is a sum of eight table lookups.
0eb4f66283da.zh: 每个段落一个浮点向量，要花256字节；十亿个段落就需要几百吉字节。Jegou、Douze 和 Schmid 2011年的乘积量化把它缩小。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个向量切成8个子向量，每个8维。<bookmark mark='b'/>在每个子向量的空间里，把所有段落聚成256组，只存下最近的那个中心的编号：1字节。向量就变成了8字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>8个位置中每个位置有256种选择，组合出天文数字般多的编码，而所需的中心却非常少。<bookmark mark='d'/>搜索不需要解压：一次性算出查询到每个中心的距离，每个段落的距离就是8次查表的和。

1ecdb1886541.en: How much does compression cost? We measured it on 64-dimensional passage vectors with a hundred queries. <bookmark mark='a'/> With two bytes per passage, PQ finds 7 percent of the true ten nearest; with eight bytes 31 percent; with sixteen, 54, at a sixteenth of the 256 bytes of the exact vector. <bookmark mark='b'/> The squared error falls from 0.66 to 0.08 of a unit vector. <bookmark mark='c'/> So real systems use the codes only for a shortlist: an inverted file picks a few clusters to scan, the codes rank their contents, and the best are re-scored exactly, as in the Faiss library.
1ecdb1886541.zh: 压缩的代价有多大？我们在64维的段落向量上用100个查询测量了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个段落2字节时，PQ 能找到真正最近的10个中的百分之7；8字节时，百分之31；16字节时，百分之54，而大小只有精确向量256字节的十六分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>平方误差从单位向量的0.66降到0.08。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以真实的系统只用这些编码来筛出一份短名单：一个倒排文件挑出几个要扫描的簇，编码给其中的内容排序，最好的那些再被精确地重新打分，就像 Faiss 库里那样。

f2b38f4b7ec3.en: Even compressed, a full scan is too slow at web scale. Malkov and Yashunin's hierarchical navigable small world graph avoids it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each point is given a random level, and the levels thin out geometrically: in our graph of 3,000 passage vectors, 2,621 live only on the bottom, and just 4 reach level 3. Each level links near neighbours, like a skip list's express lanes. <bookmark mark='b'/> A search enters at the top, walks greedily towards the query with long hops, drops a level, and repeats with shorter hops, until a beam search on the bottom level collects the nearest. <bookmark mark='c'/> A wider beam buys recall: with a beam of 40, 81 percent of the true top ten for 467 distance computations, about a sixth of brute force.
f2b38f4b7ec3.zh: 即使压缩过，在网络规模上做全量扫描也太慢了。Malkov 和 Yashunin 的分层可导航小世界图避开了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个点被赋予一个随机的层级，层级按几何级数变稀：在我们这张由3000个段落向量组成的图里，2621个只在最底层，只有4个到达第3层。每一层都连接相近的邻居，就像跳表的快速通道。<bookmark mark='b'/>搜索从顶层进入，以长跳贪心地走向查询，降一层，再以更短的跳重复，直到在最底层用一次束搜索收集最近的那些点。<bookmark mark='c'/>更宽的束换来更高的召回率：束宽为40时，找到真正前十名的百分之81，用了467次距离计算，大约是暴力搜索的六分之一。

a1b6ac87a33f.en: In practice both kinds run side by side. <bookmark mark='a'/> BM25 gives one ranking, the dense retriever another, and their scores are on unrelated scales. <bookmark mark='b'/> Reciprocal rank fusion, from Cormack, Clarke and Buettcher in 2009, ignores the scores: each list gives a passage one over sixty plus its rank, and the sums decide. Passages both lists like rise to the top. <bookmark mark='c'/> Words catch names and rare terms; vectors catch paraphrase. And on collections the encoder never saw, the BEIR benchmark of 2021 found BM25 often still hard to beat. <bookmark mark='d'/> Increasingly the reader of the top passages is a language model, as in the retrieval-augmented generation of AI, Built Part 15.
a1b6ac87a33f.zh: 实践中，两种检索并排运行。<bookmark mark='a'/>BM25 给出一个排序，稠密检索器给出另一个，而它们的分数处在互不相关的尺度上。<bookmark mark='b'/>倒数排名融合，由 Cormack、Clarke 和 Buettcher 在2009年提出，它不管分数：每个列表给一个段落60加它的排名分之一，由总和来决定。两个列表都喜欢的段落会升到顶部。<bookmark mark='c'/>词能抓住名字和罕见词项；向量能抓住同义改写。而在编码器从未见过的文档集合上，2021年的 BEIR 基准发现，BM25 往往仍然很难被超越。<bookmark mark='d'/>前几名段落的读者越来越多地是一个语言模型，就像《人工智能，从零搭建》第15部分的检索增强生成那样。

1250ced83822.en: Chapter fourteen. A search engine for the novels.
1250ced83822.zh: 第十四章：为小说打造的搜索引擎。

cc1c983e09c6.en: Here is our engine, end to end. <bookmark mark='a'/> A query arrives: the hound on the moor. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is tokenized exactly as the passages were, stop words are dropped, and the rest are stemmed, so that it matches the index's terms. <bookmark mark='c'/> The engine fetches the postings of each term. <bookmark mark='d'/> It scores the candidates with BM25, letting WAND skip those that cannot reach the top ten. <bookmark mark='e'/> And it returns the ten best passages, each with a snippet cut around the first word that matched.
cc1c983e09c6.zh: 这是我们的搜索引擎，从头到尾。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个查询到来：the hound on the moor。<bookmark mark='b'/>它和段落一样被分词，停用词被丢掉，其余的词被提取词干，这样它就能与索引的词项匹配。<bookmark mark='c'/>搜索引擎取出每个词项的倒排表。<bookmark mark='d'/>它用 BM25 给候选打分，让 WAND 跳过那些进不了前十的候选。<bookmark mark='e'/>然后返回最好的10个段落，每个都附有一段围绕第一个匹配词截取的摘要。

3d7698b30b74.en: Four queries and their best answers. <bookmark mark='a'/> The white whale, and call me Ishmael, both go to Moby-Dick, to passages where those words cluster. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pride and prejudice goes to Jane Austen's novel, and the hound on the moor to The Hound of the Baskervilles. <bookmark mark='c'/> Nothing here knows what the books are about. The ranking comes entirely from which words are rare, where they occur, and how long the passages are.
3d7698b30b74.zh: 4个查询和它们的最佳答案。<bookmark mark='a'/>the white whale 和 call me Ishmael 都指向《白鲸》，指向那些词聚集的段落。<bookmark mark='b'/>pride and prejudice 指向简·奥斯汀的那部小说，the hound on the moor 指向《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》。<bookmark mark='c'/>这里没有任何东西知道这些书讲的是什么。排序完全来自哪些词罕见、它们出现在哪里，以及段落有多长。

fe9d5483d374.en: How big is it? <bookmark mark='a'/> Our index holds 2.4 million postings. Stored as plain thirty-two-bit integers, the document ids alone take about 9.5 megabytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> As gaps in Golomb–Rice code, about 1.5, five bits a posting. <bookmark mark='c'/> And no code can do much better: choosing which f of N documents contain a term carries log of N choose f bits of information, which comes to 4.74 bits a posting here. Golomb–Rice is within a few percent of that limit, unless a code can exploit how postings cluster.
fe9d5483d374.zh: 它有多大？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的索引有2.4百万个倒排项。存成普通的32位整数，光是文档编号就要大约9.5兆字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>用 Golomb–Rice 编码存间隔，大约1.5兆字节，每个倒排项5位。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且没有任何编码能好得多：从 N 个文档中选出含有一个词项的 f 个，携带 N 选 f 的对数位信息，在这里折合每个倒排项4.74位。Golomb–Rice 与这个极限只差百分之几，除非有一种编码能利用倒排项聚集的方式。

bada9ae80468.en: And what a web search engine adds. <bookmark mark='a'/> Hundreds of billions of pages instead of eleven thousand passages, crawled again and again; hundreds of languages, with synonyms and entities; hundreds of ranking signals combined by learned models; link authority and defences against spam; thousands of machines; and news that must be searchable minutes after it is published. <bookmark mark='b'/> But the core is the same. Lucene, the open-source library under Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and Solr, ranks with BM25 by default, over compressed inverted lists like ours.
bada9ae80468.zh: 再看网络搜索引擎还要加上什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>几千亿个网页，而不是11000个段落，一遍又一遍地爬取；几百种语言，还有同义词和实体；由学习得到的模型组合起来的几百个排序信号；链接权威性和对作弊的防御；成千上万台机器；以及发布几分钟后就必须能被搜到的新闻。<bookmark mark='b'/>但核心是一样的。Lucene，Elasticsearch、OpenSearch 和 Solr 底下的开源库，默认用 BM25 排序，在像我们这样压缩过的倒排列表上进行。

b39c0fa10bc1.en: Chapter fifteen, the frontier. What should a search engine return, now that machines can write the answer?
b39c0fa10bc1.zh: 第十五章：前沿。既然机器能写出答案，搜索引擎应该返回什么？

175f4c639be9.en: Vector search is where theory lags furthest behind practice. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our own layered graph finds 68 percent of the true ten nearest passages with about 191 distance computations, and 95 percent with about 1232, against 3,000 for brute force. <bookmark mark='b'/> Graph indexes like this win the benchmarks, but they carry no worst-case guarantee: on adversarial data the greedy walk can stall far from the answer. <bookmark mark='c'/> Locality-sensitive hashing has guarantees but loses in practice, and recent theory is only beginning to explain when navigable graphs work. Closing that gap is open.
175f4c639be9.zh: 向量搜索是理论最落后于实践的地方。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们自己的分层图用大约191次距离计算，找到真正最近的10个段落中的百分之68；用大约1232次，找到百分之95；而暴力搜索要3000次。<bookmark mark='b'/>像这样的图索引赢得了各项基准测试，但它们没有最坏情况下的保证：在对抗性的数据上，贪心的遍历可能停滞在离答案很远的地方。<bookmark mark='c'/>局部敏感哈希有保证，但在实践中落败，而最近的理论才刚刚开始解释可导航图何时有效。弥合这道鸿沟是一个未解决的问题。

0fd150b2461d.en: Between words and vectors, research has found middle grounds. <bookmark mark='a'/> Learned sparse retrieval has a model rewrite each document as weighted terms, including words it does not contain, so the inverted index of this part keeps working; SPLADE, in 2021, is the best known. <bookmark mark='b'/> Late interaction keeps a vector for every token and matches them one by one at query time, as ColBERT did in 2020: more precise, and far larger. <bookmark mark='c'/> And hybrid systems simply run both, words for names and rare terms, vectors for meaning, and fuse the scores. <bookmark mark='d'/> A striking open fact: on collections a model has never seen, BM25 is often still hard to beat. Why, and how to make learned retrievers generalize, are open questions.
0fd150b2461d.zh: 在词和向量之间，研究找到了一些折中的做法。<bookmark mark='a'/>学习型稀疏检索让一个模型把每篇文档改写成带权重的词项，包括文档中并不含有的词，这样本部分的倒排索引就能继续工作；2021年的 SPLADE 是其中最知名的。<bookmark mark='b'/>延迟交互为每个词元保留一个向量，并在查询时逐一匹配它们，就像 ColBERT 在2020年所做的：更精确，也大得多。<bookmark mark='c'/>而混合系统干脆两者都运行，词用于名字和罕见词项，向量用于意思，再融合分数。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个引人注目的未解事实：在模型从未见过的文档集合上，BM25 往往仍然很难被超越。为什么，以及如何让学习得到的检索器具备泛化能力，都是未解决的问题。

725ccc986a38.en: Finally, search is changing what it is for. <bookmark mark='a'/> In retrieval-augmented generation, from AI, Built, an engine like ours finds passages and a language model writes an answer from them, with citations. The engine becomes a model's memory, and the user may never see a ranked list at all. <bookmark mark='b'/> Generative retrieval goes further: the model memorizes the collection and emits the identifiers of relevant documents itself, which makes updating the index the hard part. <bookmark mark='c'/> How to evaluate a written answer rather than a ranked list, how to check that it is faithful to its sources, and how to keep a model's memory as fresh as an index, are open.
725ccc986a38.zh: 最后，搜索的用途正在改变。<bookmark mark='a'/>在《人工智能，从零搭建》讲过的检索增强生成中，一个像我们这样的搜索引擎找出段落，由一个语言模型根据它们写出答案，并附上引用。搜索引擎成了模型的记忆，用户也许根本看不到排好序的列表。<bookmark mark='b'/>生成式检索走得更远：模型记住整个文档集合，自己输出相关文档的标识符，这让更新索引成了难点。<bookmark mark='c'/>如何评估一个写出来的答案而不是一个排好序的列表，如何检查它是否忠实于来源，以及如何让模型的记忆像索引一样保持新鲜，都是未解决的问题。

5b0c19efe631.en: Open problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> Guarantees for graph-based nearest-neighbour search on the data people actually have. <bookmark mark='b'/> Learned retrievers that beat BM25 on collections they have never seen. <bookmark mark='c'/> Evaluation when human judgments are too few, for rankings and for written answers. <bookmark mark='d'/> And generative indexes that can add and delete documents without being retrained. <bookmark mark='e'/> This part's research problem asks for a graph index with provable recall and query time on data whose intrinsic dimension is low, the case real collections seem to be.
5b0c19efe631.zh: 未解决的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>在人们实际拥有的数据上，为基于图的最近邻搜索提供保证。<bookmark mark='b'/>在从未见过的文档集合上胜过 BM25 的学习型检索器。<bookmark mark='c'/>当人工评判太少时，如何评估排序和写出的答案。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有能添加和删除文档而无需重新训练的生成式索引。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的研究题要求：在内在维度较低的数据上，也就是真实文档集合似乎所属的情形，给出一个召回率和查询时间都可证明的图索引。

71e234518c97.en: What we built in this part. Zipf's and Heaps' laws, fitted on the novels. An inverted index, and three ways to intersect its lists, from a linear merge to galloping search. Gap codes whose lengths we derived, which shrink a posting from thirty-two bits to about five. BM25, from the probability ranking principle, measured with nDCG; WAND, which finds the same top ten while fully scoring a fraction of the candidates; PageRank as the stationary distribution of a random surfer; SimHash for near-duplicates; and vectors compressed by product quantization and searched through a layered graph. One idea runs through it: a good index does almost all of the work before the query arrives.
71e234518c97.zh: 这一部分我们构建了什么。在小说上拟合的齐普夫定律和 Heaps 定律。一个倒排索引，以及求它的列表交集的三种方法，从线性合并到倍增查找。长度由我们推导出来的间隔编码，它把一个倒排项从32位缩到大约5位。从概率排序原理出发的 BM25，用 nDCG 来测量；WAND，它在只完整打分一小部分候选的情况下找到同样的前十名；作为随机冲浪者平稳分布的 PageRank；用于近似重复的 SimHash；以及用乘积量化压缩、通过分层图搜索的向量。一个思想贯穿其中：一个好的索引在查询到来之前，就完成了几乎全部的工作。

c2d6b138c6c8.en: Where this comes back. Parts 48 and 49 design a search service: how to shard it, cache it and keep it fresh. Part 50 keeps a serving system like it healthy. Part 56 returns to the eigenvectors behind PageRank with spectral graph theory. Part 57 asks when a learned ranker will generalize. And Part 60 looks at the hardware built for vector search and inference.
c2d6b138c6c8.zh: 这些内容会在哪里再出现。第48和49部分设计一个搜索服务：如何给它分片、加缓存并保持它新鲜。第50部分让像它这样的服务系统保持健康。第56部分用谱图理论回到 PageRank 背后的特征向量。第57部分会问，学习得到的排序器何时能够泛化。而第60部分着眼于为向量搜索和推理打造的硬件。

380072b05e68.en: In practice. Normalize text the way your users type it, stem with care, and keep the original words for phrase queries. Store postings sorted and compressed in blocks, with skip data and score bounds. Treat BM25 as the baseline to beat, and tune it on judged queries. Keep a set of judged queries, measure nDCG, and test significance before shipping a ranking change. And combine lexical and dense retrieval, measuring how much the approximate vector search misses.
380072b05e68.zh: 实践中。按用户输入的方式规范化文本，谨慎地提取词干，并为短语查询保留原始的词。把倒排表有序地、分块压缩地存储，附上跳跃数据和分数上界。把 BM25 当作要超越的基线，并在评判过的查询上调优它。保留一组评判过的查询，测量 nDCG，在发布一项排序改动之前先检验显著性。还有，把词法检索和稠密检索结合起来，并测量近似向量搜索漏掉了多少。

d52acd4ad131.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: give our engine block-max WAND, with a score bound for every block of postings, and measure how much more it skips. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: a graph index for nearest neighbours with guarantees on recall and speed for the kind of data people actually search.
d52acd4ad131.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。可以在任何一道上暂停。第五道是构建题：给我们的搜索引擎加上块最大 WAND，为每一块倒排项设一个分数上界，并测量它能多跳过多少。最后一道标有星号，是研究题：一个用于最近邻搜索的图索引，对人们实际搜索的那类数据，在召回率和速度上都有保证。

564798ef8888.en: Next time, Part 48: system design, and its building blocks. The numbers every designer should carry, load balancers and caches and the arithmetic of their hit rates, sharding and replication, rate limiters and queues, and how to put them together into the shape of a design.
564798ef8888.zh: 下一次，第48部分：系统设计，以及它的构件。每个设计者都应该随身带着的那些数字；负载均衡器和缓存，以及它们命中率的算术；分片和复制；限流器和队列；还有如何把它们组合成一个设计的形状。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
